name: Flair AI
tagline: Compose product scenes from cutouts, props, and generated backgrounds

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 custom model, 5 generated images and 1 video; Instant/Ad mode consumes 4x the normal image quota.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 2 videos; the official rendered page did not expose the numeric image or custom-model allowance.

tiers.name: Pro+
tiers.limits: Up to 8 standard or 2 fast custom models, 80 images and 3 videos; Instant/Ad mode costs 4x quota.

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Tier 1 includes up to 15 standard or 4 fast custom models, 150 images and 5 videos.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom model, API, security and volume terms; public price is not listed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 custom model, 5 generated images and 1 video.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual USD amounts were not exposed in the public rendered page
pricing.hiddenCosts: Instant and Ad generation modes consume 4x the normal image quota. Larger Scale allowances and API access can require higher/custom tiers.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Flair AI, compose product scenes from cutouts, props, and generated backgrounds. The hard boundary is specialized product-photo workflow, templates, model quality, and hosted rendering, plus frontier models, compute, and data.
coreLoopDIY: Compose product scenes from cutouts, props, and generated backgrounds, organize prompts and generation workflows, submit jobs to a user-owned model server, and keep outputs reproducible.
requirements: GPU-capable machine or user-supplied generation API
whatYouLose: specialized product-photo workflow, templates, model quality, and hosted rendering
replacementScope: local workflow manager, not a model replacement
ongoingBurden: GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Flair AI because the product value is the model and compute fleet, not the prompt box around it. The recurring cost buys GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Node-based open-source diffusion workflow engine with a large ecosystem.

alternatives.name: Krita AI Diffusion
alternatives.desc: Mask the product, paint the rough set and generate the background; more manual, but every layer is yours.

alternatives.name: NodeTool
alternatives.desc: Cut out the product, arrange props, relight and generate a scene in one local sketch-and-node workspace.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a local workflow manager, not a model replacement DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Flair AI in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ComfyUI as a local worker, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: compose product scenes from cutouts, props, and generated backgrounds, organize prompts and generation workflows, submit jobs to a user-owned model server, and keep outputs reproducible.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create prompt, negative-prompt, seed, dimensions, model, and workflow controls.
Submit jobs only to the local ComfyUI endpoint configured in .env.
Record exact generation parameters and workflow JSON beside every output.
Build a searchable contact sheet with compare, favorite, annotate, and rerun actions.
Support local image-to-image and mask inputs without uploading them elsewhere.
Show estimated VRAM needs and fail clearly when a workflow or model is missing.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out training a new frontier model.
Deliberately leave out copying a vendor's proprietary model or dataset.
Deliberately leave out public generation hosting and moderation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
